extracted.intended_audience: prospective NEH grant applicants, humanities organizations, scholars, and the general public interested in the NEH's mission
extracted.subtask_description: High-level description of the National Endowment for the Humanities: what the humanities are (per statute), whom NEH funds, how proposals are selected, and the agency's funding purposes and priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'humanities' (legislative)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The term 'humanities' includes, but is not limited to, the study and interpretation of the following: language, both modern and classical; linguistics; literature; history; jurisprudence; philosophy; archaeology; comparative religion; ethics; the history, criticism and theory of the arts; those aspects of the social sciences which have humanistic content and employ humanistic methods; and the study and application of the humanities to the human environment..." (legislative language quoted on the page).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statutory definition is the NEH's guiding scope: it is intentionally broad and illustrative rather than exhaustive. Project proposals should align with this conception of the humanities to be considered within NEH's mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognized humanities subject areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly listed subject examples: history, literature, linguistics, law (jurisprudence), philosophy, archaeology, language, comparative religion, ethics, the history/criticism/theory of the arts, and aspects of the social sciences with humanistic content and methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These examples indicate the kinds of scholarly and public projects NEH supports; the phrase "includes, but is not limited to" signals that other related subjects using humanistic approaches may also be appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical/eligible grant recipients (historical practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH has awarded grants to museums, historic sites, colleges and universities, K–12 teaching initiatives, libraries, public television and radio stations, research institutions, independent scholars, and to its humanities council affiliates in each of the nation’s 56 states and jurisdictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This list represents the range of organizations and individuals NEH has funded. It illustrates common applicant types but is descriptive of practice rather than a formal statement of eligibility rules (specific programs may have additional eligibility criteria).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection process: independent peer review panels
rubrics_metrics.description: Panels of independent, external reviewers examine and select top-rated proposals to receive grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH awards are competitively reviewed by external experts. Applicants should expect proposals to be evaluated by panels and should prepare materials that address expert review criteria and stand up to peer evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEH funding purposes and priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH grants support the building blocks of American civil society: helping to examine the human condition, promote civics education, understand cultural heritage, foster mutual respect for diverse beliefs and cultures, and develop media and information literacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical funded activities include bringing museum exhibitions to communities, strengthening teaching in schools, creating documentaries and podcasts, facilitating groundbreaking research, and preserving and expanding access to cultural and historical artifacts. Proposals aligned with these purposes are more likely to fit NEH priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on diversity and contemporary relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Legislative language directs attention to "reflecting our diverse heritage, traditions, and history and to the relevance of the humanities to the current conditions of national life."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH emphasizes projects that reflect diverse cultural heritage and demonstrate relevance to contemporary national life; incorporate diversity and contemporary relevance into project narratives, goals, and broader impacts where appropriate.
